title: Resumable init workers and proactive network validation probes
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: long-running init jobs in private installs were failing on transient network errors or node reboots, leaving tenant installs partially seeded and causing confusing rollback behavior. This PR adds a resumable init worker pattern and proactive network validation probes so installs can self-heal and upgrades can resume without manual intervention. Design summary: 1) Init resumer controller: a lightweight templated Job + sidecar pattern that persists step-state into a ConfigMap named redwood-init-resume-{{ .Release.Namespace }} and respects an exponential backoff TTL. Jobs include a compact resume protocol that reads the last successful step id and resumes from the next checkpoint. 2) Hook-level resume flag: values.private.init.resume.enabled and values.private.init.resume.ttlSeconds allow operators to opt-in and tune retention. 3) Network preflight probe: a templated preflight Job and probe helper that performs normalization checks (DNS resolution for control-plane endpoints, TCP connect to customer gateway IPs/CIDRs, cloud metadata reachability for onprem) and writes a structured result to a preflight ConfigMap used by the installer to gate long-running init jobs. 4) Template helpers: helpers added for templating lock ConfigMap names, backoff annotations, and idempotent job command wrappers. 5) Upgrade path: upgrade and rollback tooling will now detect resume-enabled releases and, if a previous init job failed, will schedule a fast-retry resume job instead of a full reinstall. Backwards compatibility: resume feature is opt-in and disabled by default; when disabled, behavior is identical to current hooks. Migration: operators can opt-in by setting values.private.init.resume.enabled=true and optionally configure values.private.init.networkPreflight.{enabled,targets,timeout}. Security considerations: ConfigMaps used for resume metadata are cluster-scoped within the namespace and do not contain secrets; we added RBAC rules scoped to the release ServiceAccount. Testing: included unit tests for template rendering and a small integration harness that simulates a transient network failure and demonstrates resume across a node reboot. Rollout plan: feature will be behind the values flag for one release and monitored via a new alert redwood.install.resume-failures in the SLO toolkit. See release_notes below for operator steps and caveats.

review_comments: Arjun: The backoff TTL default seems aggressive for air-gapped installs, can we make it longer by default? Author: Raised default to 86400s and added values.private.init.resume.ttlSeconds for tuning.

Lisa: Need to ensure resume ConfigMap can't be abused to inject commands. Author: The resume payload is a small JSON with step ids and checksums, we validated we never store scripts or commands. Added a schema validator in the resumer sidecar.
Tomas: Helm template lint failed on indentation for _helpers.tpl, please run helm template lint locally. Author: Fixed indentation and added unit test to cover helper rendering.
CI: integration e2e failed on first run due to flakey cloud metadata access, reran and all checks passed.
merge_result: merged via squash (commit f9e8d7c) into main
release_notes:
- Added opt-in resumable init worker pattern to reduce manual intervention after transient failures. Enable with values.private.init.resume.enabled=true.
- Added network preflight checks customizable via values.private.init.networkPreflight.targets and timeout.
- No breaking changes when disabled. Operators should test resume in a staging environment before enabling in production.
notes_for_ops: Enable with helm upgrade --set private.init.resume.enabled=true --set private.init.networkPreflight.enabled=true. Recommended to start with ttlSeconds=86400 and targets set to control-plane IPs and gateway CIDRs. Watch alert redwood.install.resume-failures and preflight metrics under installer.preflight.*.
